problem: Prior PVR studies were either broad but simulation-only (CortexBench) or narrow, small-scale hardware experiments, so it is unknown whether simulation rankings of pre-trained visual representations predict real-world robot performance.
motivation: Hardware evaluation is impractical for most researchers, so simulation is used to benchmark PVRs. That only works if sim performance predicts real performance. The authors run matched sim/real setups across 3 robots, 5 tasks, 5 PVRs and 2 learning paradigms (348 experiments, 110+ hours on hardware) to measure this.
key_idea: Build matched sim and real setups for five tasks on three robots and measure sim-to-real correlation (SRCC) of PVR-based policy performance, for both real-demo training and sim-trained zero-shot transfer.
insight: Sim predictivity is high (SRCC 0.895 with aligned sim; 0.929 in the intro) only when the sim mirrors real conditions (demo count, last-checkpoint selection, camera placement). CortexBench itself gives SRCC -0.475. Sim-trained few-shot imitation policies fail on hardware (near 0%), but large-scale RL ImageNav transfers zero-shot (VC-1 Large 90% vs 10% for from-scratch). Fine-tuning and augmentation help in both sim and real, though augmentation lowers predictivity (0.68 to 0.55) because real Open Drawer improves more than sim.
method: Task suite: matched sim/real tasks: TriFinger push cube (BC, 30 demos), Franka Reach Pos / Pick Up Bottle / Open Drawer (BC, 30/30/150 demos), Stretch ImageNav (RL in Habitat/HM3D, 600M steps).
PVR set: five PVRs (R3M, CLIP, MVP, VC-1 Base, VC-1 Large) used frozen; policies take PVR embeddings of the current image (and goal image where applicable), plus proprioception for manipulation.
Sim alignment: sim mimics the real setup (camera placement, number of demos, last checkpoint instead of best-on-validation, 42° HFOV for ImageNav), compared against CortexBench.
Sim-predictivity metric: Sim2Real Correlation Coefficient (SRCC) between sim and real success, for real-demo training and for sim-trained policies transferred to hardware.
Design-choice study: VC-1 Base/Large crossed with frozen vs fine-tuned and with/without augmentation (20% color jitter, 8px translation), giving 32 (sim, real) pairs.
Sim2Real ImageNav: RL policy trained on 800 HM3D scenes (7.2M episodes), evaluated zero-shot on 10 real episodes in an unseen apartment, with a replica of it in sim.

setting.backbone: Frozen or fine-tuned PVRs (R3M ResNet50, CLIP ViT-B, MVP ViT-L, VC-1 ViT-B/L) + policy MLP/RNN heads
setting.training_data: PVRs pre-trained on Ego4D/ImageNet etc. (pre-existing); policies trained on 30-150 demos per task (BC) or 600M-step RL on 800 HM3D scenes / 7.2M episodes for ImageNav
setting.observation: monocular RGB (plus proprioception for manipulation, goal image for ImageNav/Reach/Push)
setting.action_space: continuous joint/fingertip commands for manipulation; discrete actions for ImageNav
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D) for ImageNav, PyBullet for TriFinger, plus Franka sim; real robots
setting.privileged: none at test time (expert demos in sim use ground-truth state)

numbers.eval_set_note: 10 hand-designed episodes in one unseen real-world apartment (and its sim replica)
numbers.extra: Trained in sim only (600M steps RL on 800 HM3D scenes), real success on 10 episodes; sim replica SR 60.0
numbers.evidence: Table imagenav_only row 5: VC-1 Large sim 60.0 / real 90.0 success; real steps 122.5, DTG 0.8, collisions 1.0

numbers_note: Study paper; numbers are on the authors' own real-world ImageNav setup (not a standard benchmark). Manipulation results (real SR per PVR/task) are in Tables I, III, IV but omitted as they are not navigation.
results: Aligned sim results predict real results well when training on real demos (SRCC 0.895 vs -0.475 for CortexBench). Sim-trained few-shot IL policies fail on hardware, but large-scale RL ImageNav with frozen VC-1 Large reaches 90% real success zero-shot vs 10% for a from-scratch baseline. VC-1 Base with fine-tuning and augmentation has the best manipulation average (real 59 vs. 37-47 for the other 7 variants in Table IV).
limitations: Very small real-world evaluation sets (10 ImageNav episodes, 10 episodes per seed for Franka, 12 for TriFinger); ImageNav uses a single seed and a single real apartment.
Sim-trained imitation policies do not transfer (near 0% real) so sim2real conclusions are limited to the RL-trained ImageNav; sim was aligned only approximately, without system identification.
